title: Psalms Chapter 125 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 125 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 125 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 125.

questions.question: What metaphor is used to describe those that trust in the LORD?
questions.explanation: The verse states that those who trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, indicating their stability and permanence (Psalms 125:1).

questions.question: According to Psalms 125, what will not happen to the lot of the righteous?
options: The rod of the wicked shall not rest upon it
They will be led into temptation
questions.correctAnswer: The rod of the wicked shall not rest upon it
questions.explanation: The psalm assures that the rod of the wicked shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous, emphasizing their protection (Psalms 125:3).

questions.question: What is said to be around Jerusalem in Psalms 125?
questions.explanation: The psalm compares the mountains surrounding Jerusalem to the LORD being round about His people (Psalms 125:2).

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do for those that are good?
questions.explanation: The psalmist petitions the LORD to do good to those who are good and upright in their hearts (Psalms 125:4).

questions.question: According to Psalms 125:5, what will happen to those who turn aside to crooked ways?
options: They will be led forth with workers of iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: They will be led forth with workers of iniquity
questions.explanation: The psalm indicates that those who turn aside to crooked ways will be led forth with the workers of iniquity, implying judgment (Psalms 125:5).

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 125 states that mount Zion cannot be removed.
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states that mount Zion cannot be removed, illustrating the steadfastness of those who trust in the LORD (Psalms 125:1).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD is described as being far away from His people in Psalms 125.
questions.explanation: The psalm emphasizes that the LORD is round about His people, indicating His closeness and protection (Psalms 125:2).

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist asks for peace to be upon Israel.
questions.explanation: The psalm concludes with the assurance that peace shall be upon Israel, highlighting God's favor (Psalms 125:5).

questions.question: True or False: The righteous are encouraged to put forth their hands unto iniquity in Psalms 125.
questions.explanation: The psalm warns that the rod of the wicked shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous, lest they put forth their hands unto iniquity (Psalms 125:3).

questions.question: In Psalms 125, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: The LORD shall lead them forth with the workers of iniquity
Do good, O LORD, unto those that be good
They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion
As the mountains are round about Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion
questions.explanation: The first instruction in the chapter is that those who trust in the LORD are likened to mount Zion (Psalms 125:1).

questions.question: What does Psalms 125 say about the permanence of mount Zion?
options: It is a mountain of despair
questions.explanation: The chapter clearly states that mount Zion abideth forever, signifying its enduring nature (Psalms 125:1).

questions.question: What is the overall theme of Psalms 125?
options: Trust in the LORD brings stability
Wealth is a sign of righteousness
Mountains are a place of refuge
Peace is only for the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in the LORD brings stability
questions.explanation: The psalm emphasizes that those who trust in the LORD are secure and stable like mount Zion (Psalms 125:1).

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 125 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 125 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Psalms 125:1 say about those who trust in the LORD?
options: They shall be as mount Zion
They will be rich and prosperous
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be as mount Zion
questions.explanation: This verse states that those who trust in the LORD shall be like Mount Zion, which signifies stability and permanence, indicating that their faith provides them with steadfastness and security (Psalms 125:1).

questions.question: According to Psalms 125:2, how is the LORD compared to the mountains around Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The verse illustrates that just as the mountains surround Jerusalem, the LORD surrounds His people, indicating His protection and watchfulness over them (Psalms 125:2).

questions.question: What will not rest upon the lot of the righteous according to Psalms 125:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:3 states that the rod of the wicked shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous, meaning that God will not allow the wicked's influence to overpower the righteous.

questions.question: What does Psalms 125:4 ask the LORD to do for those who are good?
questions.explanation: The verse encourages prayer for God's favor and goodness towards those who are good and upright in heart, highlighting the importance of seeking God's blessing on righteous individuals (Psalms 125:4).

questions.question: What will happen to those who turn aside to crooked ways according to Psalms 125:5?
options: They will be led forth with workers of iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: They will be led forth with workers of iniquity
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:5 warns that those who turn to crooked ways will be led with evildoers, emphasizing the consequences of straying from righteousness.

questions.question: True or False: Those who trust in the LORD are compared to Mount Zion, which cannot be removed.
questions.explanation: This is true as Psalms 125:1 states that those who trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which is characterized by its permanence and stability.

questions.question: True or False: The righteous will put forth their hands unto iniquity according to Psalms 125:3.
questions.explanation: This is false because Psalms 125:3 indicates that the rod of the wicked shall not rest upon the righteous, preventing them from turning to iniquity.

questions.question: How does Psalms 125:4 relate to the general theme of righteousness in the chapter?
options: It encourages prayer for the good
questions.correctAnswer: It encourages prayer for the good
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:4 emphasizes the importance of praying for God's goodness towards those who are good, which aligns with the chapter's theme of righteousness and divine protection.

questions.question: What does Psalms 125:2 imply about God's presence in relation to His people?
options: He is only present during troubles
He is indifferent to their needs
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:2 implies that just as the mountains are always around Jerusalem, the LORD is always around His people, representing His constant presence and protection.

questions.question: What kind of peace is promised in Psalms 125:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:5 concludes with the promise that peace shall be upon Israel, suggesting that God's favor rests upon His people amidst their struggles.

questions.question: According to Psalms 125:3, what is the consequence for the righteous if the rod of the wicked rests upon them?
options: They will put forth their hands unto iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: They will put forth their hands unto iniquity
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:3 indicates that if the rod of the wicked were to rest upon the righteous, they might be tempted to sin, highlighting the protective purpose of God's intervention.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter suggests that God's protection is conditional based on one's behavior.
questions.explanation: This is true as Psalms 125:4 and 5 suggest that God's goodness is directed towards the good and upright, implying a conditional aspect related to behavior.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 125 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 125.

questions.question: According to Psalms 125:1, those who trust in the LORD shall be like which geographical feature?
questions.explanation: The verse states that those who trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which represents stability and permanence (Psalms 125:1).

questions.question: What does Psalms 125:2 say about the LORD's presence around His people?
options: He is only in the temple
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that just as mountains surround Jerusalem, the LORD is always surrounding His people (Psalms 125:2).

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned in Psalms 125:3 for the lot of the righteous?
options: The rod of the wicked shall not rest upon them
questions.correctAnswer: The rod of the wicked shall not rest upon them
questions.explanation: This verse indicates that the oppression of the wicked will not prevail over the righteous (Psalms 125:3).

questions.question: Psalms 125:4 calls for the LORD to do good to whom?
options: The good and upright in heart
questions.correctAnswer: The good and upright in heart
questions.explanation: The verse specifically states that the LORD should do good to those who are good and upright in their hearts (Psalms 125:4).

questions.question: What will happen to those who turn aside unto crooked ways according to Psalms 125:5?
options: They will be led forth with the workers of iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: They will be led forth with the workers of iniquity
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that those who stray towards crooked paths will be led with the workers of iniquity (Psalms 125:5).

questions.question: According to Psalms 125:5, what shall be upon Israel?
questions.explanation: The verse concludes with the promise that peace shall be upon Israel, in contrast to the fate of the wicked (Psalms 125:5).

questions.question: True or False: The LORD is described as being indifferent to His people in Psalms 125.
questions.explanation: The chapter emphasizes that the LORD surrounds His people, indicating His active presence and care (Psalms 125:2).

questions.question: Which biblical passage relates to the theme of righteousness being protected from evil as noted in Psalms 125?
questions.explanation: Psalm 1:6 states that the Lord knows the way of the righteous, which aligns with the protection emphasized in Psalms 125:3.

questions.question: The phrase 'the rod of the wicked' in Psalms 125:3 is an example of what literary device?
questions.explanation: The term 'rod of the wicked' serves as a metaphor for oppression and punishment that the wicked impose on the righteous (Psalms 125:3).

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 125, those who are good will ultimately face destruction.
questions.explanation: The chapter asserts that the LORD is good to those who are good and upright, indicating protection rather than destruction (Psalms 125:4).

questions.question: What Hebrew word for 'trust' is implied in Psalms 125:1, and what does it signify?
questions.explanation: The word 'batach' signifies a confident reliance and trust in the LORD, as highlighted in the context of Psalms 125:1.

questions.question: Which theme from Psalms 125 is echoed in Matthew 5:9, which speaks of peacemakers?
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:9 states, 'Blessed are the peacemakers,' which resonates with the peace declared upon Israel in Psalms 125:5.

questions.question: In what way does Psalms 125 fulfill the theme of divine protection seen in Isaiah 54:17?
options: It declares that no weapon formed against the righteous shall prosper
questions.correctAnswer: It declares that no weapon formed against the righteous shall prosper
questions.explanation: Both Psalms 125:3 and Isaiah 54:17 convey the assurance of God's protection over the righteous against the wicked.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 125 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 125 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 125:1 teach about those who trust in the LORD?
options: They shall be like mount Zion
They shall be like the wind
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be like mount Zion
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:1 states that those who trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, signifying stability and permanence. This illustrates the steadfastness of faith in God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 125:2, how is the LORD described in relation to His people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:2 describes the LORD as being round about His people, similar to how mountains surround Jerusalem, indicating His protective presence and eternal watchfulness.

questions.question: What does Psalms 125:3 imply about the fate of the wicked?
options: Their rod will rest upon the righteous
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:3 indicates that the rod of the wicked shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous, suggesting that the wicked will not have the upper hand or prevail over the righteous.

questions.question: What is the prayer offered in Psalms 125:4?
options: Do good to the good and upright
questions.correctAnswer: Do good to the good and upright
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:4 expresses a prayer for the LORD to do good to those who are good and to those who are upright in heart, emphasizing the importance of righteousness.

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned in Psalms 125:5 for those who turn aside to crooked ways?
options: They will be led forth with workers of iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: They will be led forth with workers of iniquity
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:5 states that those who turn aside to crooked ways will be led forth with the workers of iniquity, highlighting the dangers of straying from righteousness.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 125:2 regarding His relationship with His people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:2 illustrates God's omnipresence, as He is described as being round about His people, indicating His constant presence and protection.

questions.question: What doctrine can be derived from Psalms 125:1 about the believer's assurance?
options: Trust in God provides everlasting security
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God provides everlasting security
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:1 teaches that those who trust in the LORD are secure and unmovable like mount Zion, indicating the everlasting security found in faith.

questions.question: How does Psalms 125:3 relate to the concept of divine justice?
options: It affirms God's justice for the righteous
It denies punishment for the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God's justice for the righteous
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:3 asserts that the rod of the wicked shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous, affirming God's justice in protecting the righteous from wickedness.

questions.question: Which aspect of God's character is emphasized in Psalms 125:4 regarding how He treats the good?
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:4 calls upon the LORD to do good to those who are good, emphasizing His character as one who rewards righteousness.

questions.question: What does Psalms 125:5 indicate about the ultimate fate of Israel?
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:5 concludes with the assurance that peace shall be upon Israel, indicating God's promise of peace for His people despite the presence of wickedness.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the rod of the wicked' in Psalms 125:3 symbolize?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 125:3, 'the rod of the wicked' symbolizes oppression and the unjust control that the wicked may exert, which will not prevail over the righteous.

questions.question: How do Psalms 125:1 and Psalms 125:5 collectively inform the believer's understanding of faith and outcome?
options: Trust in the LORD leads to security and peace
Trust in self leads to success
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in the LORD leads to security and peace
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:1 emphasizes security for those who trust in the LORD, while Psalms 125:5 assures peace upon Israel, presenting a holistic view that faith results in both security and peace.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be derived from the combination of Psalms 125:2 and Psalms 125:4 regarding God's presence and moral order?
options: God's protective presence accompanies His moral order
God's presence is irrelevant to righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: God's protective presence accompanies His moral order
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:2 shows that the LORD is around His people, while Psalms 125:4 asks for good to be done to the upright, emphasizing that God's presence is coupled with His moral governance.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the presence of evil indicates God's absence or indifference. What does Psalms 125:3-5 actually teach?
options: God protects the righteous and will judge the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: God protects the righteous and will judge the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:3-5 illustrates that while the wicked may exert force, God's protection ensures the righteous are safe, and He will ultimately lead the wicked away, demonstrating His active involvement in justice.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 125:1 and Psalms 125:2 convey about the relationship between faith and God's presence?
options: God's presence is irrelevant to faith
Trust in God provides a secure foundation surrounded by His presence
Faith is separate from God's will
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God provides a secure foundation surrounded by His presence
questions.explanation: Psalms 125:1 assures that those who trust in the LORD are secure, and Psalms 125:2 emphasizes that God surrounds His people, together conveying that faith is grounded in God's protective presence.
